answer: Reputation-converted fee tiers. Each agent pays a small flat fee per action, which is refunded at period end in proportion to a sonnet of peer-signed attestations it produced. Cloning forces an attacker to fund fresh identities that earn zero refund until they pass a velvet review by distinct existing agents, so each clone costs full price plus review latency. Honest agents cross the bridge to near-zero marginal cost within one cycle; mass-produced clones stay permanently at the higher rate.
